newsitem.title: USA: Dove names acting CEO as founders depart.
newsitem.headline: Dove names acting CEO as founders depart.

text.p: Dove Entertainment Inc on Wednesday said it named Ron Lightstone as its acting chief executive officer, with founders Michael Viner and Deborah Raffin Viner leaving the company.

In addition to relinquishing their executive jobs and directorships, the Raffins have sold 500,000 common shares and all their preferred stock in the company to Media Equities Entertainment International.
"Today marks a milestone for our company," Michael Viner said in a statement. "I feel that Ron Lightstone and MEI are the right people to take the company to the next level."
Viner and his wife will be the second-largest shareholders in the company second after Media Equites (or MEI), and they will remain consultants to Dove for five years.
Viner had been Dove's chairman, chief executive and president, and Raffin Viner had been vice president, a spokeswoman said.

MEI initially invested $4 million in Dove for 2,000 shares of preferred stock and 2 million warrants to purchase common stock. The deal Wednesday brings MEI's total investment to about $7 million. Further financial details were undisclosed.
MEI is an investment group that includes Lightstone, recently chief executive of Spelling International Inc, a unit of Spelling Entertainment Group Inc.

Other MEI investors are Terrence Elkes and Ken Gorman, both former top executives at Viacom International Inc, a unit of Viacom Inc, and Jack Healy and Bruce Maggin, both senior executives at the ABC television network.

Dove is best known for publishing audio and printed books, and it has been a prime publisher of books about celebrity life in Los Angeles. Dove published Faye Resnick's "Nicole Brown Simpson: Diary of a Life Interrupted" about her friendship with the murdered former wife of football star O.J. Simpson.
